title: Shooting a Pass from Behind
description: Shooters catch passes coming from behind them — from a baseline drive or an offensive rebound — and turn their body to the rim in one motion before shooting.

content.objective: Catch a pass coming from behind the body and turn square to the rim without wasting time.
content.setup: Passer on the baseline near the block; shooter at the wing facing the rim.
instructions: The shooter waits at the wing with the hands ready.
The passer passes from the baseline, behind the shooter's line of sight.
The shooter turns the head to see the ball and opens the hips toward it.
Catch with the inside foot forward, swing the hips to the rim and shoot.
Repeat at the top and the other wing.
coachingPoints: Open the hips to see the ball early.
Turn on the catch with a pivot, not a hop.
Ball goes straight into the pocket.
commonMistakes: Catching blind with the back to the passer.
content.safety: Shooters rebound their own ball only when the lane is clear; nobody stands under the rim while others shoot.
regressions: Passer stands to the side, not fully behind.
content.gameApplication: Many kick-outs and offensive-rebound passes come from behind the shooter.
